recipes.name: Easy, Speedy Corn Muffins
ingredients_raw: 2 (8.5 ounce) packages dry corn muffin mix

steps.text: Gather all ingredients and preheat oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C). Lightly grease the bottoms only of 12 muffin cups, or line with baking cups.

Place the eggs in a large bowl, and beat until light colored. Stir in the canned corn and sugar until well blended. Add the muffin mixes, and stir just until dry ingredients are moistened. The batter will be lumpy.
Bake in preheated oven until toothpick inserted in center of a muffin comes out clean, 16 to 22 minutes. Cool 5 minutes in pan, then turn out on a rack.

raw_recipe.headline: Easy, Speedy Corn Muffins
raw_recipe.description: Making corn muffins won't get easier than this streamlined method using prepared muffin mix, canned cream-style corn, and a tad of brown sugar. Enjoy them warm or at room temperature.

review.reviewBody: Great tasting corn bread, very moist and rich. I made these as muffins and they were done in 15 minutes. I also made this recipe in a in a 9x12 baking pan and that baked for around 8 extra minutes. (see my 2 photos) It's so easy to make. The best ever!

I liked these muffins. Used regular muffin pan and filled them full and it made 15 muffins. 
I used 1/2 teaspoon less salt and 1/4 cup sugar. I would let the cornmeal sit in the hot batter longer as I felt they were a little gritty. I cooked them 14 minutes and they were a little more done then I would like but any less time they didn't brown.

I added 1/2 C shredded cheddar cheese. Also, after filling 2/3 of the cups, I added 1/2 of a minced jalapeño to the batter before filling the remaining cups and marked the pepper muffins with a slice of jalapeño. These were well recieved at a friend’s chili party.

I’ve used this recipe a few times and love it.
Great with a couple of changes. First, you have to add the milk (per the Jiffy box). Second, I always add about 1/4 cup sugar per Jiffy box. It makes ALL the difference! Moist and yummy!

These corn muffins were very good and easy. I used Jiffy Corn Muffin mix and left out the brown sugar. This recipe make a lot of batter! I was worried that two boxes of mix would not fit in one muffin pan. The muffin cups were filled to the top (not the 2/3 full the recipe calls for) and all of the batter fit (barely). The muffins had a nice "muffin top" and were very yummy, gooey, sweet (the sugar was not missed) and popular. I will definitely make this again!
Tasted great and easy to make. I beat the eggs by hand and it was enough to puff up the entire thing. The 9x13 version does NOT take 40 minutes (?!?) to bake. Try 20 or less.

5.23.22 They’re correctly titled because they really are easy and speedy to make. I’m not a fan of sweet cornbread, but that small amount of brown sugar leaves a hint of sweetness, just enough. The only thing I will do differently in the future is spray the entire muffin cup instead of just greasing the bottom. I have really good quality, non-stick muffin tins, and these muffins didn’t exactly pop out, even running a knife around the edge. Adding corn to cornbread is a favorite of mine, and I was quite satisfied with the way this turned out. Not quite as good as from scratch cornbread, but close enough!
I made it with double the brown sugar. It was moist and delicious! I will make it again.

Wonderful recipe. I doubled the recipe to accommodate the 12 people at the pot luck. I was out of buttermilk so I added a can of evaporated milk and 1 cup of 2% milk. I also used safflower oil in instead of plain vegetable. They came out great. I brushed melted sweet cream butter mixed with honey on the tops as they came out of the oven. The double recipe produced 18 muffins and a 8-inch pan. They were a hit.

I made this cornbread for Thanksgiving & it was a hit!!!! I added about 1 tsp baking powder so it would rise & not be to thin. I also used the confetti style cream corn instead of the plain. It was delicious.

Made as mini-muffins for a child's birthday to go with chicken chili. Made one batch with the sugar and one without - no noticeable difference in flavor so next time I will leave out the sugar. The recipe made 36 mini-muffins. I baked the muffins @ 400 degrees for 11 minutes. Everyone loved these moist corn muffins.
They were amazing. Nice and moist
Made exactly like the recipe.They were excellent.
No changes - great as is!!!

Great recipe, I added a splash of milk. Served with venison chili to a group and everyone enjoyed the muffins. Moist and just the right amount of sweetness. Will save this, it will be my go to corn muffin from now on. Thank you!

We made these for a crowd of 80 incarcerated men we serve with in a prison ministry. They LOVED them!! They are so moist and crispy on the outside. We're doing them again this month by popular request! Thanks for an awesome, easy, inexpensive recipe!! We found the ingredients very inexpensively at Aldi.
YES very good ,made many times my go to recipe for muffins
My kids have never liked corn muffins with corn in them they prefer the packages mix lol this time they loved it and the cream style corn was a huge hit
These are delicious and very easy. I was looking for some muffins that are low in sugar and still tasty. They are also extremely moist!
Followed the recipe exactly, these muffins turned out moist and delicious and were so easy to make.
